edges.description: The deeper staphylococcal or streptococcal pyoderma produces ulceration rather than remaining a purely subcorneal process.
Skin infection with nephritogenic GAS M serotypes can initiate the immune-mediated renal branch of disease.
The dermal infection inflames the skin around the ulcer, giving the elevated red margin that often surrounds ecthyma lesions.
Impaired neutrophil recruitment lets GAS lesion growth and local tissue injury outpace the early cellular response.

edges.description: Dermal ulceration is the defining tissue morphology of ecthyma.
Exudate from the ulcerated dermal lesion dries into the crust covering the ulcer.
Loss of dermis in the ulcer heals by scar formation.
Post-streptococcal immune injury to the glomeruli presents clinically as acute glomerulonephritis.

nodes.description: When ecthyma is caused by nephritogenic S. pyogenes M serotypes, immune responses to skin infection can be followed by acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
